adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 35.7. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price is 5.5% above regular (10.25), which historically correlates with lower demand. Past price increases (no promotions) show a median 6% drop vs baseline; the noise-adjusted effect is x0.94. The classical uplift model suggests no effect, but that ignores price. The recent week (2026-09-21) sold 35 units at regular price, near baseline. No post-promo dip observed. The price hike is the only driver. Evidence is moderate (2 past price spikes), so shrink effect toward 1.0. Downside spread increases slightly due to price uncertainty.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
